120	They knew nothing, but if HaShem wants it, "not by might and not by power, but by My spirit, says HaShem." Wasn't it so
121	on Chanukah?
122	With the few, the very few Maccabees, they took the swords and lifted the sword,
123	and the sword fought by itself. How could it be that eighteen or however many
124	Maccabee kohanim, weak ones, who worked in the Temple service, as the Gemara says in Tractate Shekalim, page 13,
125	weak kohanim are irritable, to this day kohanim are irritable. Why
126	irritable?
127	Because they would walk on a marble floor barefoot, since it is forbidden to go up to the Temple Mount with shoes.
128	The Gemara says in Tractate Chagigah, page 4: everyone is obligated to appear, who is exempt? Whom
129	does it come to exempt? It comes to exempt the pampered, those who are spoiled, who want to go up to the Temple Mount with
130	shoes.
131	About them it is written: "Who asked this of you, to trample My courtyards?"
132	Go up to the Temple Mount, take off your shoes.
133	It is a holy place: "Remove your shoes from your feet."
134	So that is how one must go up. Today we do not go up to the Temple Mount under any circumstances, but it is destined to come, speedily
135	in our days, and when we go up to the Temple Mount, all the shoes will be outside.
136	It is not, it is siyata dishmaya, there will be no smell of shoes.
137	Once I went to pray in the Old City, and on the way, on Shechem Road, there is a huge mosque.
138	So I passed through the mosque to reach the Kotel, in the Old City, Shechem Gate.
139	What a smell of shoes there was, socks with mold and fungus.
140	"Fear and dread shall fall upon them." What a stench! On the Temple Mount
141	there was nothing like that. People would take off their shoes. It was siyata dishmaya, a miracle, and everyone
142	would go up to the Temple Mount. So now, what happened? Moshe Rabbeinu went out
143	and came to take the whole land of Og and of
144	Sichon. He took everything. After he took everything, Og,
145	king of Bashan, came out. Hey, didn't you get it? The first one fell, do you want to fall too?
146	Who gave the people of Israel the strength to bring Sichon down?
147	The Holy One, blessed be He. The swords they grasped, the Shechinah lifted them. They had to make the effort
148	of lifting a sword. What would happen?
149	"Not by might and not by power, but by My spirit, says HaShem." They said, for the sake of the unification of the Holy One and His Shechinah,
150	"We are coming to fight Sichon the wicked, and his army, and all his land.
151	May it be Your will, Master of the Worlds, give us siyata dishmaya."
152	They grasped the sword, and the sword lifted them.
153	As the Gemara says about the Ark of Israel: the Ark carried those who carried it.
154	So it was with the sword.
155	Do you think people lifted the Ark with the Tablets of the Covenant in the desert?
156	Of course not!
157	They would lift the poles, the badim, those two poles around it. They would lift the poles,
158	and it was like a bus, like a cable car, wow, and they, they are in the air, and it
159	carries them. The Ark carries its bearers. So it was with this sword. They would lift
160	the swords. Moshe Rabbeinu, who was an elder sitting in the yeshivah, do you think he did weights every day
161	and exercises and taught them? Of course not!
162	He taught them Torah. So how did they defeat the whole army of Sichon?
163	Who said, "And so be it"? Did HaShem not command?
164	When they held the sword, the sword was heavier than his hand, he could not lift it.
165	That one went to do like this with the sword, tak, it fell on his beard, and cut off his beard.
166	Once I was at the home of a rabbi, a great person whom I respect, in Brooklyn.
167	I was clean-shaven then, so I was ashamed to come to him clean-shaven.
168	Now, I did not shave because I wanted to shave. I shaved because the shaving machine
169	had problems and somehow got stuck in the middle and caught some of the hair, so I said, since it has gone this far, let it go all the way, and I took off the beard.
170	What could I do?
171	Now to come to such a rabbi with a shaved beard, what will he think of me, a Reform rabbi?
172	What will he say about me?
173	So first of all I asked him for forgiveness and pardon: Rabbi, I shaved, know that it was like this, it was beyond
174	my control, "oness rachmana patrei," one under duress is exempt.
175	He said to me, it's fine, Rav Meir, it's fine, something like that happened to me once too.
176	I said to him, a shaving machine got stuck on you too?
177	He tells me, no, worse.
178	I said to him, what?
179	He says, at the search for chametz, I was checking for chametz with the candle, suddenly I see fire, flames.
180	His whole beard went up in flames.
181	How careful one must be with this.
182	He had a beautiful, big beard, he tells me, years until I grew it out.
183	It all went up in flames.
184	So one must be careful.
185	In any case...
186	How did they manage to break Sichon?
187	The Holy One, blessed be His Name.
188	Then they took the swords, the swords ran by themselves, tak, tak, tak, suddenly they did
189	a somersault.
190	Moshe, do effects, Moshe.
191	How was it again?
192	Great, you only love the nonsense.
193	So that's it, that is how it was, they finished off all of Sichon.
194	Sichon went, he and all his people, may their memory be a curse.
195	Now, after that, came Og the wicked.
196	Now Og was more wicked than Sichon, he was tall, a giant.
197	And Og is the refugee who came to Avraham Avinu, whom Avraham circumcised.
198	This is what is written here at the end of last week's Parashah.
199	"Do not fear him, for I have given him into your hand, and all his people, and you shall do to him as you did to Sichon king of the Amorites."
200	What is "do not fear him"?
201	The sign of his covenant. Fear, he is protected, he has a covenant.
202	So HaShem said to Moshe: do not fear him, the sign of the covenant of circumcision he has, do not be afraid that he is
203	protected.
204	"For I have given him into your hand," I am placing him in your hands.
205	Why indeed did the covenant of circumcision not protect him?
206	Why did the covenant not protect him?
207	After all, the covenant protects the body like a mezuzah protects a house.
208	Because only when the mezuzah is kosher does it protect the house.
209	If he blemishes the covenant, the covenant does not protect him.
210	On the contrary, it becomes a burden to him.
211	"Come close to me, please," as Yosef says to his brothers, "and HaShem made me a lord, Elokim,
212	ruler over all Egypt."
213	What is "come close, please"?
214	With all due respect, he lowered the, the trousers, and showed them his covenant of circumcision, he told them he is circumcised,
215	with great perfection.
216	So writes Rashi: circumcised.
217	Everyone is circumcised, even gentiles have circumcised ones. To this day in England there is Queen Elizabeth the third or fourth, one of those,
218	who took and they cut their children, gentiles, they perform circumcision on them. So what
219	proof is it that he is circumcised? Rather, he showed them that the Name of HaShem shines on his covenant of circumcision.
220	Whoever guards his covenant of circumcision, the Name of HaShem shines on the covenant and his whole body is protected
221	from harmful forces, from destructive angels, from evil women, he is protected from everything. Why?
222	Because he has the Name of HaShem shining. Moshe did not see the Name of HaShem shining on Og, but he knew he was circumcised.
223	He did not see it. Had he seen it, he would have seen that there is no Name of HaShem.
224	He said, he heard about him that he is circumcised.
225	The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: do not fear him, I have given him into your hand.
226	Og: "And Og king of Bashan went out toward them, he and all his people, to battle, at Edrei."
227	Were they Moroccans?
228	The Edri family?
229	Edri?
230	Edri.
231	"And they struck him and his sons and all his people until no survivor was left to him,
232	and they possessed his land."
233	They possessed his land.
234	So the two mightiest armies in the world at that time were Sichon and Og.
235	Who struck Og?
236	Og was a giant. Moshe Rabbeinu took a staff, a stick, took the staff, and with
237	the staff he leapt onto the ground with both his knees, struck with both his feet on Og's knees,
238	and brought Og down.
